## Why visit

Liverpool’s great pub spectacle: room after room of carved wood, decorative ceilings, glass, mosaic and marble. The pleasure is in moving beyond the first bar and examining how differently the smaller rooms and large rear space are treated. This is an architectural essential even if another pub wins your personal beer-of-the-day contest. Its position opposite the Philharmonic Hall also makes it a natural meal or concert-adjacent stop. Do not rush the visit simply because it is famous; the craftsmanship rewards patient inspection.

## Beer

CAMRA confirms cask ale. Nicholson’s operates the pub; choose from the actual board rather than expecting a particular guest.

## Food

British pub menu and pies from Nicholson’s; booking a meal is sensible around performances.

## Plan the visit

Grade I listed; CAMRA three-star historic interior. For the famous marble toilets, ask staff about viewing and respect users’ privacy.

**Getting there:** Hope Street; combine on foot with Roscoe Head, Ye Cracke, Belvedere and Peter Kavanagh’s.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
